objective: Identify vulnerabilities and unauthorised configuration change across the in-scope environment and drive them to resolution within defined timeframes, so that known weaknesses do not persist unaddressed.
description: Authenticated vulnerability scanning runs on a defined cadence against the full in-scope asset inventory, covering hosts, container images, and dependencies. Findings are risk-ranked and automatically raised as tickets carrying a remediation deadline derived from severity. Deadlines that cannot be met are escalated and either extended with documented approval or formally risk-accepted by an authorised owner with an expiry date.

conditions: The service organization operates infrastructure or software within the system boundary

implementation_guidance: Drive scan scope from the authoritative asset inventory, and reconcile scanned assets against it. Scope narrower than the inventory is the most common defect in this control.
Use authenticated scanning where possible; unauthenticated scans understate exposure.
Define severity-based remediation timeframes in policy and enforce them with an SLA clock on the ticket.
Make risk acceptance an explicit, authorised, time-bounded artifact rather than an unremediated ticket left open.
Cover container images and third-party dependencies, not only host operating systems.
design_considerations: Is scan coverage defined by an authoritative inventory rather than a static target list?
Are remediation timeframes defined, and by whom were they approved?
Is there a defined path for exceptions, or does the process silently tolerate overdue items?
operating_considerations: Did scans run on cadence for every period, with no unexplained gaps?
Were remediation timeframes met, and where missed, was there documented approval?
Did scanned coverage match the asset inventory at each point in the period?

evidence_examples.note: Scan results with asset coverage and remediation tracking through to closure.

risks.description: A known, publicly exploitable vulnerability remains in production beyond the window in which it is actively exploited.
Assets outside scan scope carry unknown exposure that no process is positioned to detect.

source_refs.supports: Identity of the criterion this control is intended to help meet.
Scan scope versus asset inventory as the dominant point of auditor challenge.
Recommended use of authenticated scanning and time-bounded risk acceptance.

notes: Monthly cadence and severity-based timeframes are organizational choices. The criteria do not specify scan frequency or remediation SLAs; the organization defines them and is then held to what it defined.
Added as a third exemplar control so that the vulnerability scan evidence object required by the evidence data model has a valid control to reference. See framework/metadata.json decision SD-006.
questionnaire_questions populated in the CC7 phase. The control predates the questionnaire model and had no question coverage; QN-OPS-001-Q07 closes that.
